key_insight: WaspMOT fills a major benchmark gap in multi-object tracking by testing whether models can keep identities consistent over very long time spans, not just short clips. It uses long-duration Trichogramma wasp sequences to reveal tracking failures that standard datasets often miss.
problem_solved: Existing MOT benchmarks are mostly built from short video sequences, so they do not properly evaluate long-term identity preservation. This paper addresses the need for a dataset that measures sustained tracking performance over extended ecological experiments.
method: Introduces WaspMOT, a benchmark for long-term multi-object tracking in controlled wasp experiments.
Provides 10 long video sequences, each around 12,000 frames, to stress-test identity consistency over time.
Focuses on Trichogramma wasps, creating a specialized setting for evaluating tracking under prolonged, realistic conditions.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, WaspMOT offers a more demanding and realistic evaluation setting for MOT systems. It helps identify whether trackers can maintain identity over long horizons, which is crucial for robotics, ecology, and other real-world monitoring tasks.

paper_title: WaspMOT: A Benchmark for Long-Term Multi-Object Tracking of Trichogramma Wasps
paper_authors: Tomasz Stanczyk, Yuan Gao, Hardik Agarwal, Seongroo Yoon, Tiantao Zhang
